newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Chelyabsvyazinform telecom eyes new issue.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Chelyabsvyazinform telecom eyes new issue.

text.p: Russian telecoms holding company Svyazinvest has agreed in principle to allow its subsidiary Chelyabsvyazinform to issue new shares, a Chelyabinsk official said on Thursday.
Sergei Akimenko, a deputy chief executive at the regional telecom, said the issue would double the number of ordinary shares but would probably not take place until 1998.

"Svyazinvest agreed in principle to a secondary issue and we must now prepare our financial plan," he said, adding Svyazinvest had agreed on the condition that the size of its stake, 56.34 percent of voting stock, was preserved.
"We doubt the issue will be earlier than next year," Akimenko said. A state-held stake must be sold before the new issue can take place, and shareholders must approve it.
Akimenko said the company, located east of the Urals mountains at the edge of Siberia, would issue domestic bonds this year, but he gave no further details.
Many Russian regional telecoms are eager to expand and improve their networks but lack funds and have little hope of receiving resources from Svyazinvest, a government-owned holding.

Shares in Chelyabsvyazinform, formally known as Svyazinform Chelyabinskoi Oblasti, are traded on the RTS-2 market of relatively illiquid shares. Shares closed at $56.00 on Wednesday. It was $51.50 in mid-February.
